key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant because point defects in the gap do not produce strong enough Shockley-Read-Hall recombination to explain device losses.
engineering_relevance: This supports t-Se as a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where defect tolerance can simplify materials optimization.
method: First-principles calculations on a large, chemically diverse set of point defects
Quantified both radiative and nonradiative SRH recombination rates
Examined dependence on defect level, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping
evidence_signal: The abstract reports multiple deep gap levels, but recombination is strongly suppressed by large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per event.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on computed defect behavior, so real devices may still be limited by defects outside the modeled set or by processing-related microstructure effects.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
